clue.text: In at core working hours for speed of response

indicators.note: working here means being worked over, so the letters of these three words are rearranged

parts.note: hours are a measure of time, so the word stands for it

explanation.surface: Someone's typical turnaround during office hours, measured as a speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges IN AT CORE into REACTION.
explanation.definitionFit: This compound is the interval before a person responds, which is the measure of how quickly they respond.

clue.text: Conductor having died caused upset

indicators.note: having means taking on, so the next piece is added at the end

parts.note: Sir Simon Rattle is a British conductor

explanation.surface: An orchestra conductor's death caused distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' might suggest electricity; it is Simon Rattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Being rattled means being flustered or unsettled, which is upset in the adjective sense.

clue.text: Area right inside planet's infernal regions

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so the right goes into the planet

parts.note: Venus is a planet

explanation.surface: A region of a planet holds some hellish zones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts R into VENUS.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman myth this lake near Naples was the entrance to the underworld, and the name came to mean hell itself.

clue.text: Do myth differently — enquire within for dramatist

indicators.note: within means placed inside the rearranged letters
differently means done another way, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: to ask is to enquire

explanation.surface: A playwright is told to retell a myth another way, asking questions along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' rearranges DO MYTH into THOMYD, and 'within' sets the question word in it. Kyd wrote The Spanish Tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the Elizabethan author of The Spanish Tragedy, a writer of plays.

clue.text: Person in saddle having slim advantage?

definitions.meaning: a rider on a horse is said to be up, so one rider is the phrase
being a single point ahead of a rival

explanation.surface: A jockey with a narrow lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A jockey mounted is 'up', and being a step ahead of someone is the same phrase.

clue.text: Painter sends second one to bottom, caught in sinking ship

indicators.note: the second one, the letter I, is moved down to the end of the painter's name

parts.note: Titian was a Venetian Renaissance painter
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An artist sends a second person to the seabed, caught on a sinking vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: TITIAN becomes TITANI when its second I goes to the end; 'one' is I.
explanation.definitionFit: This liner famously sank on its maiden voyage in 1912 after hitting an iceberg.

clue.text: Change of heart for parrot with sailor in taxi

indicators.note: the heart, the central letter, is changed for another

parts.note: to parrot is to mimic
AB is an able seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor travels in a cab with his pet parrot, which has a change of heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parrot' is the verb: MIMIC, whose central M becomes N.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a car for hire that has to be booked by phone, unlike a cab hailed in the street.

clue.text: Ideal spot, as sullied, Tempter at last having entered?

definitions.text: Ideal spot, as sullied, Tempter at last having entered?

indicators.note: having entered means the letter has gone in among the others
sullied means spoilt, so the letters are mixed up
at last means take the final letter

explanation.surface: Eden, the perfect place, spoiled once the serpent had got in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sullied' rearranges IDEAL SPOT AS; 'having entered' puts R, from 'at last' on Tempter, among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's epic tells how Satan entered Eden and the ideal garden was spoilt by the Fall.

clue.text: Cunning Italian author pens note in style

indicators.note: to pen is to shut in, so the cunning author encloses the note

parts.note: cunning means craft or artfulness, as in art
Umberto Eco was an Italian novelist
D is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A crafty Italian writer jots down a note in his own manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pens' puts D inside ARTECO, between the T and the E.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is that of a decorative design movement of the 1920s and 30s, an example of a style.

clue.text: Capitalist's banking on old money that's obsolete

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the banks go at the end

parts.note: ex means former or old
tin is British slang for money

indicators.note: the two banks of the word are its outermost letters

explanation.surface: A financier relies on old cash that is now out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banking' takes the outside letters C and T of Capitalist; 'on' puts them after EXTIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something that no longer exists or is no longer in use, as with a dead species.

clue.text: About to get in there and study Romeo's play

indicators.note: to get in means to go inside, so about enters the word there

parts.note: CA, circa, means about
to take a subject is to study it
R is Romeo in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone is told to get there and study the play Romeo and Juliet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get in' places the circa abbreviation in the middle of 'there'. 'Romeo' looks like Shakespeare's hero; it is just the radio-alphabet R.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Pinter's 1960 drama about a tramp in a London house is a famous play.

clue.text: City worker going through map book endlessly

indicators.note: going through means passing inside, so one piece sits within the other
endlessly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: an atlas is a book of maps
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: An employee leafs through a road atlas while travelling to a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the final S, and 'going through' sets the insect worker inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of the US state of Georgia is a large city.

clue.text: Spirit delivers one from pain and hunger

indicators.note: to deliver from is to free, so the one is released from the word pain

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to ache for something is to hunger for it

explanation.surface: A spirit, perhaps a stiff drink, rescues someone from pain and hunger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivers' takes I out of PAIN, leaving PAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash and verve are both meanings of the word, as is spirit in the sense of liveliness.

clue.text: Asian runner in French south retired

indicators.note: retired means going back, so the French word is read backwards

parts.note: sud is French for south

explanation.surface: An Asian athlete has retired to the south of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns SUD into DUS. 'Runner' looks like an athlete; it is a river.
explanation.definitionFit: This great river flows through Pakistan, and in crosswords a runner is often a river.

clue.text: Hooded killer from Royal Horse Artillery

parts.note: a king is a royal
a cob is a sturdy kind of horse
RA is the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: A masked assassin emerges from the Royal Horse Artillery regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Horse Artillery is a real British army unit, which hides the split into three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This venomous snake spreads a hood when threatened, and its bite kills.

clue.text: Whereof perhaps, as I long, a time's recalled internally?

definitions.text: Whereof perhaps, as I long, a time's recalled internally?

indicators.note: internally means placed inside the rearranged letters
whereof can be read as of where, a place unfixed, and perhaps adds doubt, so the letters are rearranged
recalled means called back, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: T is short for time

explanation.surface: A wistful musing on past days, recalled from within as one yearns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whereof perhaps' rearranges AS I LONG into NOSLGIA; 'recalled' turns AT into TA; 'internally' puts it after NOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Wistful longing for the past is exactly what the clue's picture of recalled times describes.

clue.text: Foul residue covers irrational tragedian

indicators.note: covers means wraps round, so the rearranged letters enclose the other piece
foul means fouled up, signalling the letters are mixed

parts.note: pi is the best-known irrational number

explanation.surface: Nasty muck coats a deranged actor of tragic roles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foul' rearranges RESIDUE into EURIDES, and 'covers' wraps those letters round the number. 'Irrational' looks like an adjective for the tragedian; it is pi.
explanation.definitionFit: He was one of the three great tragic playwrights of ancient Athens.

clue.text: Elizabeth's favourite beer in privilege curtailed

indicators.note: in means the beer goes inside the shortened word
curtailed means the tail, the last letter, is cut off

parts.note: a right is a privilege
ale is a beer

explanation.surface: The Queen's favourite drink is beer, a privilege now cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' cuts the last letter off, and 'in' puts the beer inside. Elizabeth is the first Queen Elizabeth, not the recent one.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter, explorer and courtier, was a famous favourite of Queen Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Author at Ephesus, discontented, seeks household god

parts.note: a pen writes, so it stands for an author, as in pen-name

indicators.note: discontented means losing the contents, leaving only the outside letters

explanation.surface: A writer at the ancient city of Ephesus, unhappy, looks for a domestic deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discontented' leaves ES from Ephesus. The answer is a plural standing for a collective household deity.
explanation.definitionFit: These were the Roman gods of the larder and home, each a household god.

clue.text: Come together in lake, shipping gallons

indicators.note: shipping means taking aboard, so the lake takes in the other piece

parts.note: a mere is a lake

explanation.surface: Boats meet up on a lake, loading gallons of fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shipping' puts G inside MERE.
explanation.definitionFit: To combine or unite is to come together, as two companies or roads do.

clue.text: Silver mesh installed in second generator

indicators.note: installed in means set inside the other piece

parts.note: MO, a moment, is a second
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
net is a mesh

explanation.surface: A silver gauze is fitted inside a backup power unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'installed in' puts AGNET inside MO.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small machine that uses permanent magnets to make electric current, a kind of generator.

clue.text: Band composer requires an organ case

parts.note: a rib is a band or strip, as in a ribbed knit
John Cage was an American composer

explanation.surface: A band's composer needs a case for his organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests the instrument; it is the heart and lungs.
explanation.definitionFit: This bony frame encloses the heart and lungs, a protective housing for organs.

clue.text: Shakespearean character's men get nothing

parts.note: OR is short for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
to land something is to get it
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare figure's soldiers come away with nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is': the character is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the hero of As You Like It, who falls for Rosalind in the Forest of Arden.

clue.text: Bond I'd play now and then in unusual fashion

indicators.note: now and then means at intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: An actor says he would play James Bond in an unusual style now and again.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means strangely or in a peculiar way.

clue.text: Subject is Gable: Tortured Artist

indicators.note: tortured means twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A tormented painter is the topic of a study of the actor Clark Gable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tortured' rearranges GABLE into ALGEB.
explanation.definitionFit: This branch of mathematics is a school subject.

clue.text: Pressman after dance becomes contorted

indicators.note: after means the press figure follows the dance

parts.note: the twist is a 1960s dance
ED, short for editor, is a newspaper man

explanation.surface: A journalist ends up all bent out of shape after a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean bent or wrung out of normal shape.

clue.text: Pineapple class to admit unmarried chaps

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the class encloses the other piece

parts.note: a grade is a class or rank

indicators.note: M is the abbreviation for married, so unmarried chaps lose it

parts.note: chaps are men, fellows

explanation.surface: A school class on pineapples lets in some single men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unmarried' leaves EN, as M is the abbreviation for married; 'to admit' sets it in the class. Pineapple is old soldiers' slang, from the ridged casing.
explanation.definitionFit: Pineapple is old military slang for a hand bomb, from its ridged shape.

clue.text: Showgirl Kay exploding with energy in film

indicators.note: exploding means blowing apart, so the letters are scattered and reformed

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A showgirl named Kay bursts onto the stage full of energy in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploding' rearranges SHOWGIRL KAY plus E.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a 1949 Ealing comedy about islanders salvaging a cargo of Scotch.
